prompt: What is a common practical use of Java reflection in frameworks?
choices: To make code run faster by bypassing the JIT compiler
To discover and wire together classes (dependency injection, ORM mapping, JSON serialization) without compile-time coupling
To prevent other classes from accessing private fields
To replace the JVM's class loader
explanation: Spring uses reflection for dependency injection. Jackson uses it to map JSON to Java fields. JUnit uses it to find and call @Test methods. Reflection allows frameworks to work with user classes without knowing them at compile time, but at the cost of compile-time safety and some performance overhead.
